findings.reason: The protected source is already the canonical one-pass bijection check. Its inverse maps reject both possible mapping conflicts, its length guard prevents truncation by zip, and its names expose the two directions directly. It is concise and interview-quality, so no candidate is justified.

Metadata consistently identifies public LeetCode problem 290 and its Python two-string-to-boolean contract. The Reference states the full bijection semantics, preserves the three source examples in order and the sole source explanation, and retains all six constraints concerning lengths, characters, and spacing.

The immutable native source remains tied to verified submission 2064311783. It and the app-local source have identical tokenization, length rejection, inverse maps, aligned traversal, conflict checks, assignments, and successful return; only the required class wrapper and type syntax differ.

The former benchmark used digit-bearing words forbidden by the lowercase-only source contract. Legal 16/64/264-position tiers now repeat the lowercase word wa with a matching repeated pattern, span 16.5x, and force a correct pairwise-consistency implementation through all comparisons. The current source passes at -0.01 relative exponent and 1.01x largest ratio; the quadratic control passes every output but fails only scaling at +1.25 and 90.26x.

The manifest now includes the storage retained by sentence splitting instead of claiming only distinct-map space. The Approach defines n as total input characters, accounts for aggregate word hashing, proves both directions of the bijection, and distinguishes pairwise checking, a one-way map, length mismatch, and valid repetition.

The hash-bound public Reference remains verified against its reviewed source evidence, preserving all three examples and their explanation presence, all six constraints, the exact bijection semantics, and the zero-visual structure.
